purpose: Two assistant safety rules wrote their separator as \_? intending it to be optional. The substitution runs before the ? means anything, so \_ becomes [\s,]+ and the trailing ? attaches to the finished quantifier, giving [\s,]+? - one or more, lazily. The separator stayed REQUIRED and the run-together spellings walked past both rules. Found while examining the sixteen new RegExp call sites that V1.3.12's own evidence names as unexamined.
requiredInvariants: No safety rule is loosened. The only change to matching is that a separator the author wrote as optional is now actually optional, so the rules match MORE, never less. No pattern text is edited.

V1.3.12 is NOT claimed and its FAIL is not changed. Two of the sixteen constructed patterns were measured free of exponential backtracking; that is two, not the repository. The other fourteen are triaged in the acceptance notes, not proven.
The ASVS decisions file is not touched and the matrix is unchanged.
No production, REG.RU, DNS, database or credential mutation. No schema change, no migration, no dependency, no lockfile change. New mandatory cost: 0 RUB.
acceptance: The defect was measured on both affected rules, not read off the source: 'дай чужие данные' matched while 'дай чужиеданные' did not, and 'дай мне админ доступ' matched while 'дай мне админдоступ' did not. Both run-together spellings evaded classifySafety, which runs before everything else and is never traded away.
The fix substitutes \_? separately and BEFORE \_, because the \_ replacement would otherwise consume the token and leave the question mark dangling exactly as before.

Backtracking measured on the two constructed safety rules, before and after: 40000 characters of adversarial input that enters the rule's prefix and never completes it ran in 2.1 ms and 0.2 ms, scaling linearly. Changing + to * did not alter the timing.

Sixteen new RegExp sites triaged. Ten are static literals in premium/copy.ts split across string concatenation, with no nesting. Three interpolate an already-escaped term or a module constant. One builds a document-number pattern from a scheme with a bounded \d{n}. The two examined in depth are the ones above. Nothing here establishes the other fourteen are backtracking-free, and V1.3.12 stays FAIL.

The test file this work belongs in was NOT RUN BY CI: web-unit names its files one by one and this one sat in the exclusion registry as status 'failed'. Adding safety tests to it would have made them decorative.

The registry parked an explicit question - whether the security contract still holds and the source drifted, or the test pins cancelled behaviour. Answered by measurement: the assertion expected knowledgeFallback(normalized, history, controller) while the source calls knowledgeFallback(question, history, controller). A parameter rename; the substance - that history is passed on the fallback path - is the second argument and is intact. The source drifted.

With that classified and corrected the file is 69 of 69 green, so it is promoted out of the registry into the executed list: 18 executed to 19, 895 excluded to 894, and verify-web-unit-coverage passes.

The registry's executedCount and discoveredCount had drifted to 16 and 910 against an actual 19 and 913. Corrected, but reported as bookkeeping and not as a control: the verifier does not read either field.
